# pickers API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Native SPFx picker fields with JSON selection ownership and shared pane lifecycle.

Native SPFx picker option and direct-array property contracts.

## PropertyPaneContentTypePicker

Native Property Pane content type picker, sharing the React control's options, source and presentation.
Omitted scope reads the owning site collection root; list scope requires a toolkit list selector.
Forwards the React control's filters, local complete-catalog search and defaults. Selection never provisions a content type or enables list content types.
The host owns apply/persistence; arrays contain validated JSON references, including in single selection.
Same owner/key/DOM updates preserve root, selection/query state and equivalent request cache.
Initial unlabeled selections use selection-control AutoSkeleton during hydration; available labels stay visible. Search/refresh and later updates do not restart the skeleton.
The native field supplies its own matching WebPart provider, renderer and pane theme. Do not wrap it in JSX or mount it under a React provider yourself. Configure native resource mappings for the inherited React control. Existing host authentication and delegated permissions still govern queries.
Equivalent native renders preserve pending nonreactive drafts. Changing `valueRevision` explicitly adopts `value`; hydration never emits property changes. Invalid values or a missing native change callback disable mutations and display a diagnostic. Latest-factory disposal releases resources; stale disposal cannot unmount its replacement.
Inherited option defaults, source restrictions and asynchronous validation/error callbacks follow [ContentTypePicker](../controls/pickers.md#contenttypepicker); native persistence notification remains separate.

### Imports

```ts
import { PropertyPaneContentTypePicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
```

### Use when

- A native SPFx configuration pane must persist ContentTypePickerValue JSON references using the same query and validation options as the React picker.

### Avoid when

- Rendering a picker in ordinary React content; use the corresponding React control and its selection callback instead.

### Throws

- Error - The target property is empty, nested or prototype-related, or the field key is blank.

### Examples

#### Native ContentType picker

```ts
import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import type { IPropertyPaneConfiguration } from '@microsoft/sp-property-pane';
import { PropertyPaneContentTypePicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
import type { ContentTypePickerValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/pickers';

interface Properties { values?: ContentTypePickerValue[]; }
export default class SelectionWebPart extends BaseClientSideWebPart<Properties> {
  public render(): void {
    this.domElement.textContent = `${this.properties.values?.length ?? 0} saved references`;
  }
  protected getPropertyPaneConfiguration(): IPropertyPaneConfiguration {
    return { pages: [{ groups: [{ groupName: 'Selection', groupFields: [
      PropertyPaneContentTypePicker('values', {
        instance: this, key: 'content-type-field', value: this.properties.values ?? [],
        label: 'Content types', scope: 'list', list: 'Projects',
      }),
    ] }] }] };
  }
}
```

#### Select native content type references

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button } from '@fluentui/react-components';
import type { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import type { IPropertyPaneConfiguration } from '@microsoft/sp-property-pane';
import { PropertyPaneContentTypePicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
import type { ContentTypePickerValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/pickers';

interface SourceProperties { pickerContentTypes?: ContentTypePickerValue[]; }
interface NativePropertyPaneEnvironment<P extends object> {
  readonly instance: BaseClientSideWebPart<P>;
  readonly readProperties: () => P;
  readonly refresh: () => void;
}
interface NativePropertyPaneController {
  readonly getConfiguration: () => IPropertyPaneConfiguration;
  readonly fieldChanged: (propertyPath: string, oldValue: unknown, newValue: unknown) => void;
  readonly configurationComplete: () => void;
  readonly changesApplied: () => void;
  readonly dispose: () => void;
}
interface NativePropertyPanePreparation { readonly release: () => void; }
type NativePropertyPanePreparationResult =
  | { readonly status: 'prepared'; readonly lease: NativePropertyPanePreparation }
  | { readonly status: 'blocked'; readonly reason: string };
interface DemoPropertyPanePort<P extends object> {
  readonly prepare: (create: (host: NativePropertyPaneEnvironment<P>) => NativePropertyPaneController) => NativePropertyPanePreparationResult;
}
interface DemoRegions {
  controls?: React.ReactNode;
  commands?: React.ReactNode;
  status?: React.ReactNode;
  diagnostics?: React.ReactNode;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
}
function createContentTypeController(host: NativePropertyPaneEnvironment<SourceProperties>): NativePropertyPaneController {
  return {
    getConfiguration: () => ({ pages: [{
      header: { description: 'Select saved content type references, then use native Close. Reset is not native Discard.' },
      groups: [{ isGroupNameHidden: true, groupFields: [
        PropertyPaneContentTypePicker('pickerContentTypes', {
          instance: host.instance, key: 'picker-content-types', value: host.readProperties().pickerContentTypes ?? [], label: 'Content types', scope: 'site',
        }),
      ] }],
    }] }),
    fieldChanged: () => {},
    configurationComplete: () => {},
    changesApplied: () => {},
    dispose: () => {},
  };
}

// The initialized host owns actual native Edit/Close and SDK persistence.
// This structural port is private example tooling. Configure the ordinary native
// recipe's localization resources; existing host authentication and permissions
// govern queries. The factory installs its own WebPart provider and renderer.
// Site scope resolves the initialized web's owning collection root; no list is needed.
export function Demo({ render, resetRevision = 0, propertyPane }: {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  propertyPane?: DemoPropertyPanePort<SourceProperties>;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState('Prepare before opening this WebPart’s actual native property pane.');
  const [saved, setSaved] = React.useState<string>();
  const lease = React.useRef<NativePropertyPanePreparation>();
  const readProperties = React.useRef<(() => SourceProperties)>();
  const lifetime = React.useMemo(() => ({ active: true }), [propertyPane, resetRevision]);
  const previousRevision = React.useRef(resetRevision);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (previousRevision.current === resetRevision) return;
    previousRevision.current = resetRevision;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
    setSaved(undefined);
    setStatus('Local state reset. A produced native session survives until its real native lifecycle ends; Reset is not Discard or rollback.');
  }, [resetRevision]);
  React.useEffect(() => () => {
    lifetime.active = false;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
  }, [lifetime]);
  const prepare = (): void => {
    if (!propertyPane || !lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    lease.current?.release();
    const result = propertyPane.prepare(host => {
      readProperties.current = host.readProperties;
      return createContentTypeController(host);
    });
    if (result.status === 'blocked') {
      lease.current = undefined;
      setStatus(result.reason);
      return;
    }
    lease.current = result.lease;
    setStatus('Prepared. Open this WebPart’s actual native Edit property pane, select Content types, then use native Close. Preparing does not open the pane or query.');
  };
  const observe = (): void => {
    if (!lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const read = readProperties.current;
    if (!read) { setStatus('Open the prepared native scenario before inspecting its saved values.'); return; }
    setSaved(JSON.stringify(read().pickerContentTypes ?? [], undefined, 2));
  };
  const regions: DemoRegions = propertyPane ? {
    commands: <><Button onClick={prepare}>Prepare native scenario</Button><Button onClick={observe}>Inspect saved content type references</Button></>,
    status: <p role="status">{status}</p>,
    children: <><p>Use the actual native Edit and Close controls. Selection, preparation and Reset do not open or close the pane. Reset cancels only an unproduced preparation and local observations; it cannot discard accepted native changes.</p><p>If the SDK, React or host fails after native configuration was returned, reload before further native scenario work; automatic recovery is unsupported.</p></>,
    diagnostics: <pre>{saved ?? 'Use Inspect saved content type references after an actual native selection.'}</pre>,
  } : {
    status: <p role="status">The initialized native scenario host is not connected. This selected native scenario is not active.</p>,
    children: <p>This WebPart’s actual native Edit still opens the existing full integrated configuration independently of the selected entry until the final native cutover. There is no enabled Prepare action here. Selection and Reset do not query or open the pane.</p>,
  };
  return render ? render(regions) : <>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</>;
}
export const demo = { host: 'webPart', kind: 'read', contentPlacement: 'configuration', hostAdapter: 'propertyPane', observe: "Prepare the native ContentType picker, open this WebPart's actual Edit property pane, select content type references and use native Close and inspect the saved JSON; selection and Reset do not open the pane or query." };
```

```tsx
// The initialized host owns actual native Edit/Close and SDK persistence.
// This structural port is private example tooling. Configure the ordinary native
// recipe's localization resources; existing host authentication and permissions
// govern queries. The factory installs its own WebPart provider and renderer.
// This example deliberately chooses list fields. The Field API also permits
// omitted list for site columns; the prerequisite here is not an API requirement.
export function Demo({ render, resetRevision = 0, propertyPane }: {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  propertyPane?: DemoPropertyPanePort<SourceProperties>;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState('Prepare before opening this WebPart’s actual native property pane.');
  const [listTitle, setListTitle] = React.useState('');
  const [saved, setSaved] = React.useState<string>();
  const lease = React.useRef<NativePropertyPanePreparation>();
  const readProperties = React.useRef<(() => SourceProperties)>();
  const lifetime = React.useMemo(() => ({ active: true }), [propertyPane, resetRevision]);
  const previousRevision = React.useRef(resetRevision);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (previousRevision.current === resetRevision) return;
    previousRevision.current = resetRevision;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
    setListTitle('');
    setSaved(undefined);
    setStatus('Local state reset. A produced native session survives until its real native lifecycle ends; Reset is not Discard or rollback.');
  }, [resetRevision]);
  React.useEffect(() => () => {
    lifetime.active = false;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
  }, [lifetime]);
  const prepare = (): void => {
    if (!propertyPane || !lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const list = listTitle.trim();
    if (!list) { setStatus('Enter a real exact list title before preparing.'); return; }
    // Freeze this chosen configuration; later draft edits do not alter the native session.
    lease.current?.release();
    const result = propertyPane.prepare(host => {
      readProperties.current = host.readProperties;
      return createFieldController(host, list);
    });
    if (result.status === 'blocked') {
      lease.current = undefined;
      setStatus(result.reason);
      return;
    }
    lease.current = result.lease;
    setStatus('Prepared. Open this WebPart’s actual native Edit property pane, select Fields, then use native Close. Preparing does not open the pane or query.');
  };
  const observe = (): void => {
    if (!lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const read = readProperties.current;
    if (!read) { setStatus('Open the prepared native scenario before inspecting its saved values.'); return; }
    setSaved(JSON.stringify(read().pickerFields ?? [], undefined, 2));
  };
  const regions: DemoRegions = propertyPane ? {
    controls: <>
      <label>Exact list title<Input aria-label="Exact list title" value={listTitle} onChange={event => setListTitle(event.target.value)} /></label>
      <p>Enter an existing exact list title in the initialized current web; even a GUID-looking string is a title. Draft collection and preparation perform no queries.</p>
    </>,
    commands: <><Button disabled={!listTitle.trim()} onClick={prepare}>Prepare native scenario</Button><Button onClick={observe}>Inspect saved field references</Button></>,
    status: <p role="status">{status}</p>,
    children: <><p>Use the actual native Edit and Close controls. Selection, preparation and Reset do not open or close the pane. Reset cancels only an unproduced preparation and local observations; it cannot discard accepted native changes.</p><p>If the SDK, React or host fails after native configuration was returned, reload before further native scenario work; automatic recovery is unsupported.</p></>,
    diagnostics: <pre>{saved ?? 'Use Inspect saved field references after an actual native selection.'}</pre>,
  } : {
    status: <p role="status">The initialized native scenario host is not connected. This selected native scenario is not active.</p>,
    children: <p>This WebPart’s actual native Edit still opens the existing full integrated configuration independently of the selected entry until the final native cutover. There is no enabled Prepare action here. Selection and Reset do not query or open the pane.</p>,
  };
  return render ? render(regions) : <>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</>;
}
```

```tsx
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
    setListTitle('');
    setTextField('Title');
    setSaved(undefined);
    setStatus('Local state reset. A produced native session survives until its real native lifecycle ends; Reset is not Discard or rollback.');
  }, [resetRevision]);
  React.useEffect(() => () => {
    lifetime.active = false;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
  }, [lifetime]);
  const prepare = (): void => {
    if (!propertyPane || !lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const list = listTitle.trim();
    const field = textField.trim();
    if (!list || !field) { setStatus('Enter a real exact list title and its verified internal display field before preparing.'); return; }
    // Freeze this chosen configuration; later draft edits do not alter the native session.
    lease.current?.release();
    const result = propertyPane.prepare(host => {
      readProperties.current = host.readProperties;
      return createListItemController(host, list, field);
    });
    if (result.status === 'blocked') {
      lease.current = undefined;
      setStatus(result.reason);
      return;
    }
    lease.current = result.lease;
    setStatus('Prepared. Open this WebPart’s actual native Edit property pane, select Items, then use native Close. Preparing does not open the pane or query.');
  };
  const observe = (): void => {
    if (!lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const read = readProperties.current;
    if (!read) { setStatus('Open the prepared native scenario before inspecting its saved values.'); return; }
    setSaved(JSON.stringify(read().pickerItems ?? [], undefined, 2));
  };
  const regions: DemoRegions = propertyPane ? {
    controls: <>

      <label>Verified internal display field<Input aria-label="Verified internal display field" value={textField} onChange={event => setTextField(event.target.value)} /></label>
      <p>Enter an existing exact list title in the initialized current web; even a GUID-looking string is a title. Verify that this list has the chosen internal display field; Title is only an initial suggestion. Draft collection and preparation perform no queries.</p>
    </>,

    status: <p role="status">{status}</p>,

Reset cancels only an unproduced preparation and local observations; it cannot discard accepted native changes.</p><p>If the SDK, React or host fails after native configuration was returned, reload before further native scenario work; automatic recovery is unsupported.</p></>,
    diagnostics: <pre>{saved ?? 'Use Inspect saved item references after an actual native selection.'}</pre>,
  } : {
    status: <p role="status">The initialized native scenario host is not connected. This selected native scenario is not active.</p>,
    children: <p>This WebPart’s actual native Edit still opens the existing full integrated configuration independently of the selected entry until the final native cutover. There is no enabled Prepare action here. Selection and Reset do not query or open the pane.</p>,
  };
  return render ? render(regions) : <>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</>;
}
```

## PropertyPaneListPicker

Native Property Pane List picker, sharing the React control's options, source and presentation.
The host owns apply/persistence; arrays contain validated JSON references, including in single selection.
Same owner/key/DOM updates preserve root, selection/query state and equivalent request cache.
Initial unlabeled selections use selection-control AutoSkeleton during hydration; available labels stay visible. Search/refresh and later updates do not restart the skeleton.
The native field supplies its own matching WebPart provider, renderer and pane theme. Do not wrap it in JSX or mount it under a React provider yourself. Configure native resource mappings for the inherited React control. Existing host authentication and delegated permissions still govern queries.
Equivalent native renders preserve pending nonreactive drafts. Changing `valueRevision` explicitly adopts `value`; hydration never emits property changes. Invalid values or a missing native change callback disable mutations and display a diagnostic. Latest-factory disposal releases resources; stale disposal cannot unmount its replacement.
Inherited option defaults, source restrictions and asynchronous validation/error callbacks follow [ListPicker](../controls/pickers.md#listpicker); native persistence notification remains separate.

### Imports (4)

```ts
import { PropertyPaneListPicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
```

### Use when (4)

- A native SPFx configuration pane must persist ListPickerValue JSON references using the same query and validation options as the React picker.

### Avoid when (4)

- Rendering a picker in ordinary React content; use the corresponding React control and its selection callback instead.

### Throws (4)

- Error - The target property is empty, nested or prototype-related, or the field key is blank.

### Examples (4)

#### Native List picker

```ts
import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import type { IPropertyPaneConfiguration } from '@microsoft/sp-property-pane';
import { PropertyPaneListPicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
import type { ListPickerValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/pickers';

interface Properties { values?: ListPickerValue[]; }
export default class SelectionWebPart extends BaseClientSideWebPart<Properties> {
  public render(): void {
    this.domElement.textContent = `${this.properties.values?.length ?? 0} saved references`;
  }
  protected getPropertyPaneConfiguration(): IPropertyPaneConfiguration {
    return { pages: [{ groups: [{ groupName: 'Selection', groupFields: [
      PropertyPaneListPicker('values', {
        instance: this, key: 'list-field', value: this.properties.values ?? [],
        label: 'List',
      }),
    ] }] }] };
  }
}
```

```tsx
interface NativePropertyPaneEnvironment<P extends object> {

interface NativePropertyPaneController {

  readonly fieldChanged: (propertyPath: string, oldValue: unknown, newValue: unknown) => void;

interface NativePropertyPanePreparation { readonly release: () => void; }
type NativePropertyPanePreparationResult =

  | { readonly status: 'blocked'; readonly reason: string };
interface DemoPropertyPanePort<P extends object> {

  status?: React.ReactNode;
  diagnostics?: React.ReactNode;
  children?: React.ReactNode;
}
function createListController(host: NativePropertyPaneEnvironment<SourceProperties>): NativePropertyPaneController {
  return {
    getConfiguration: () => ({ pages: [{
      header: { description: 'Select saved list references, then use native Close. Reset is not native Discard.' },
      groups: [{ isGroupNameHidden: true, groupFields: [
        PropertyPaneListPicker('pickerLists', {

        }),
      ] }],
    }] }),
    fieldChanged: () => {},
    configurationComplete: () => {},
    changesApplied: () => {},
    dispose: () => {},
  };
}

Reset cancels only an unproduced preparation and local observations; it cannot discard accepted native changes.</p><p>If the SDK, React or host fails after native configuration was returned, reload before further native scenario work; automatic recovery is unsupported.</p></>,
    diagnostics: <pre>{saved ?? 'Use Inspect saved list references after an actual native selection.'}</pre>,
```

## DistributiveOmit

Remove React-owned selection members independently from each source branch, preserving source discriminants such as ContentTypePicker scope/list.

Source-owned support type; no public named import.

- `K`: Property names removed from every branch.

```ts
type DistributiveOmit<T, K extends PropertyKey> = T extends unknown ? Omit<T, K> : never
```

## PickerPropertyKey

Safe direct property names whose array element domain exactly matches the selected JSON reference type.
Optional and readonly arrays are accepted. Scalar, mixed, untyped, unknown and narrower element domains, nested paths and prototype-related names are rejected. The native factory still receives an array for single selection; pass [] for an absent optional property.

## PropertyPanePickerProps

Property Pane emits JSON value arrays, never raw UI models or only renderer keys.
The SPFx change callback receives accepted values; the host owns property updates and apply/persistence. The control does not persist values.
initialOptions and availableOptions stay distinct. Values removed from availableOptions remain selected.
Stable root/client/query runtime is preserved on prop updates, and original unresolved references are retained.
Available labels remain visible during hydration. Initial selections without display labels/models use AutoSkeleton only for the selection control region until initial hydration settles; later searches, refreshes and updates do not reactivate it.
Empty selections and mixed selections with known labels keep the normal control. Real terminal errors remain visible; no property is rewritten by hydration.
Inherits the React picker's accessible-name check: JSX/object labels require explicit
aria-label or aria-labelledby; otherwise supply a nonblank plain string label.
In default change mode, validateSelection can veto an action before a value is emitted.
Blur mode validates already committed ordinary gestures without reverting them; explicit ID
resolution still validates before emission. validationMessage overrides only displayed text.
Historical presentation combobox renders Dropdown with popup search; its trigger remains mounted through hydration.
Popup search and selection clear are separate. Blur validation runs after leaving the entire field and owned popup.
Selected tags stay in TagPicker rather than being duplicated in popup rows; colorfulTagAvatars affects tags only.
The native provider uses the initialized instance; callers do not install a second provider around the field. React `selectedOptions`, `defaultSelectedOptions`, `defaultPrincipals` and `onOptionSelect` are removed. Remaining React source, Field slots, callbacks, filtering, selection cardinality and defaults remain unchanged. Those callbacks retain their React semantics and do not acknowledge native persistence.

### Imports (6)

```ts
import type { PropertyPanePickerProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
```

### Native pane theme and lifetime

All native picker fields, including the file/folder field, read tokens from the custom-field container in its owning document, independently of the web-part section theme. Usable opaque hex/comma-RGB surface and foreground anchors select a matching neutral light/dark base; remaining usable tokens overlay that base. An unavailable snapshot retains the same container's last valid theme, or neutral light before the first valid snapshot. Equivalent snapshots retain identity. Body-mounted menus/dialogs share this bridge. No network, persistent cache or polling is involved.
Native renders, host theme notifications, ancestor/reparenting changes and observed stylesheet replacement/text/load events refresh the snapshot without remounting. Unsignalled CSSOM-only changes need a host notification or another native render. Disposal releases observers, listeners and scheduled frames.
Same owner/key/DOM renders retain the React 17 root and provider; a changed owner/key replaces that session. Only the latest rendered factory may dispose it. Metadata cache leases are scoped to owner/document; closing the last field clears memory, so a later opening starts fresh. Separate roots can initialize clients independently. This does not guarantee tenant authorization or native Apply behavior.

```ts
import type { PropertyPanePickerProps, SitePickerProps, SitePickerValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
type Properties = { sites?: SitePickerValue[] };
export function siteOptions(instance: BaseClientSideWebPart<Properties>, value: readonly SitePickerValue[]): PropertyPanePickerProps<Properties, SitePickerProps, SitePickerValue> {
  return { instance, key: 'sites', value, label: 'Sites' };
}
```

```ts
    /** Required initialized web-part instance supplying context, clients and lifecycle ownership. Never serialized into the property value. */
  readonly instance: BaseClientSideWebPart<TProperties>;
    /** Required nonempty stable native field key within the owning web part. Never encode selection, query or time. */
    readonly key: string;
    /** Required complete ordered JSON references, even for single selection; pass [] for an undefined optional host property. Invalid updates preserve the last confirmed selection and disable mutation until valid values arrive. */
    readonly value: readonly TValue[];
    /** Explicitly adopt value and clear a pending nonreactive draft, even when its contents equal old props.
     * Initially omitted/undefined or unchanged revision preserves the draft when value is equivalent. Every revision change, including removal to undefined, adopts value without remounting or refreshing equivalent queries.
     */
    readonly valueRevision?: string | number;
  }
```

```tsx
function createPrincipalController(host: NativePropertyPaneEnvironment<SourceProperties>): NativePropertyPaneController {

export function Demo({ render, resetRevision = 0, propertyPane }: {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  propertyPane?: DemoPropertyPanePort<SourceProperties>;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState('Prepare before opening this WebPart’s actual native property pane.');
  const [saved, setSaved] = React.useState<string>();
  const lease = React.useRef<NativePropertyPanePreparation>();
  const readProperties = React.useRef<(() => SourceProperties)>();
  const lifetime = React.useMemo(() => ({ active: true }), [propertyPane, resetRevision]);

    previousRevision.current = resetRevision;

    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
    setSaved(undefined);
    setStatus('Local state reset. A produced native session survives until its real native lifecycle ends; Reset is not Discard or rollback.');
  }, [resetRevision]);

    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
```

## PropertyPaneSitePicker

Native Property Pane Site picker, sharing the React control's options, source and presentation.
The host owns apply/persistence; arrays contain validated JSON references, including in single selection.
Same owner/key/DOM updates preserve root, selection/query state and equivalent request cache.
Initial unlabeled selections use selection-control AutoSkeleton during hydration; available labels stay visible. Search/refresh and later updates do not restart the skeleton.
The native field supplies its own matching WebPart provider, renderer and pane theme. Do not wrap it in JSX or mount it under a React provider yourself. Configure native resource mappings for the inherited React control. Existing host authentication and delegated permissions still govern queries.
Equivalent native renders preserve pending nonreactive drafts. Changing `valueRevision` explicitly adopts `value`; hydration never emits property changes. Invalid values or a missing native change callback disable mutations and display a diagnostic. Latest-factory disposal releases resources; stale disposal cannot unmount its replacement.
Inherited option defaults, source restrictions and asynchronous validation/error callbacks follow [SitePicker](../controls/pickers.md#sitepicker); native persistence notification remains separate.

### Imports (8)

```ts
import { PropertyPaneSitePicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
```

### Use when (6)

- A native SPFx configuration pane must persist SitePickerValue JSON references using the same query and validation options as the React picker.

### Avoid when (6)

- Rendering a picker in ordinary React content; use the corresponding React control and its selection callback instead.

### Throws (6)

- Error - The target property is empty, nested or prototype-related, or the field key is blank.

#### Supply a known native site-reference label

```tsx
import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import { PropertyPaneSitePicker } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/property-pane/pickers';
import type { SitePickerValue } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/pickers';
interface Properties { sites?: SitePickerValue[] }
// Place the returned field in the initialized host's groupFields. The host still owns persistence.
function knownSiteField(instance: BaseClientSideWebPart<Properties>, values: SitePickerValue[]) {
  return PropertyPaneSitePicker('sites', {
    instance, key: 'sites', label: 'Sito', hint: 'Seleziona una raccolta siti',
    value: values.map(site => site.url === 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/marketing'
      ? { ...site, text: 'Marketing' } : site),
  });
}
```

```tsx
export function Demo({ render, resetRevision = 0, propertyPane }: {
  render?: (regions: DemoRegions) => React.ReactElement;
  resetRevision?: number;
  propertyPane?: DemoPropertyPanePort<SourceProperties>;
}): React.ReactElement {
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState('Prepare before opening this WebPart’s actual native property pane.');
  const [listTitle, setListTitle] = React.useState('');
  const [saved, setSaved] = React.useState<string>();
  const lease = React.useRef<NativePropertyPanePreparation>();
  const readProperties = React.useRef<(() => SourceProperties)>();
  const lifetime = React.useMemo(() => ({ active: true }), [propertyPane, resetRevision]);
  const previousRevision = React.useRef(resetRevision);
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (previousRevision.current === resetRevision) return;
    previousRevision.current = resetRevision;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
    setListTitle('');
    setSaved(undefined);
    setStatus('Local state reset. A produced native session survives until its real native lifecycle ends; Reset is not Discard or rollback.');
  }, [resetRevision]);
  React.useEffect(() => () => {
    lifetime.active = false;
    lease.current?.release();
    lease.current = undefined;
    readProperties.current = undefined;
  }, [lifetime]);
  const prepare = (): void => {
    if (!propertyPane || !lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const list = listTitle.trim();
    if (!list) { setStatus('Enter a real exact list title before preparing.'); return; }
    // Freeze this chosen configuration; later draft edits do not alter the native session.
    lease.current?.release();
    const result = propertyPane.prepare(host => {
      readProperties.current = host.readProperties;
      return createViewController(host, list);
    });
    if (result.status === 'blocked') {
      lease.current = undefined;
      setStatus(result.reason);
      return;
    }
    lease.current = result.lease;

  };

    if (!lifetime.active || resetRevision !== previousRevision.current) return;
    const read = readProperties.current;

    setSaved(JSON.stringify(read().pickerViews ?? [], undefined, 2));
  };
  const regions: DemoRegions = propertyPane ? {
    controls: <>
      <label>Exact list title<Input aria-label="Exact list title" value={listTitle} onChange={event => setListTitle(event.target.value)} /></label>
      <p>Enter an existing exact list title in the initialized current web; even a GUID-looking string is a title. Draft collection and preparation perform no queries.</p>
    </>,
    commands: <><Button disabled={!listTitle.trim()} onClick={prepare}>Prepare native scenario</Button><Button onClick={observe}>Inspect saved view references</Button></>,
    status: <p role="status">{status}</p>,
    children: <><p>Use the actual native Edit and Close controls. Selection, preparation and Reset do not open or close the pane. Reset cancels only an unproduced preparation and local observations; it cannot discard accepted native changes.</p><p>If the SDK, React or host fails after native configuration was returned, reload before further native scenario work; automatic recovery is unsupported.</p></>,
    diagnostics: <pre>{saved ?? 'Use Inspect saved view references after an actual native selection.'}</pre>,
  } : {
    status: <p role="status">The initialized native scenario host is not connected. This selected native scenario is not active.</p>,
    children: <p>This WebPart’s actual native Edit still opens the existing full integrated configuration independently of the selected entry until the final native cutover. There is no enabled Prepare action here. Selection and Reset do not query or open the pane.</p>,
  };
  return render ? render(regions) : <>{regions.controls}{regions.commands}{regions.status}{regions.children}{regions.diagnostics}</>;
}
export const demo = { host: 'webPart', kind: 'read', contentPlacement: 'configuration', hostAdapter: 'propertyPane', observe: "Prepare the native View picker, open this WebPart's actual Edit property pane, select view references and use native Close and inspect the saved JSON; selection and Reset do not open the pane or query." };
```
